To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have devised an efficient object prediction technique that allows reducing the performance and energy overheads of object detection in Autonomous Driving systems, while keeping the accuracy of object detection comparable to that of the original object prediction.

IntPred: (i) is the first work to leverage object interpolation in the context of autonomous driving; (ii) achieves comparable accuracy with respect to the original detection; (iii) is able to reduce the computational requirements by 70%, allowing to increase the frame processing rate; (iv) is applicable to any DNN based object detection algorithm.
IntPred is an object prediction technique that, by leveraging on the stability of objects over time, allows saving more than 75% of the computations of the original object detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions: 1.

the design and evaluation of IntPred, a flexible, accurate and fast object detection technique for automotive applications, and its integration into a state-of-the-art autonomous driving software stack.

(i) a thorough study on the impact of interpolation on object detection accuracy in autonomous driving systems; (ii) a novel interpolation algorithm tailored for object detection, that exploits the fact that objects do not move much across frames; (iii) a new framework that leverages IntPred to consolidate additional applications onto a platform.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work provides a novel and efficient way for object interpolation, which can be applied to a wide variety of domains, including automotive.

our technique allows to achieve the same accuracy of object detection in the same time, with a 4x reduction of energy and a 4.6X improvement in the frame rate, with respect to the original DNN based object detection approach, and a 2X reduction in the number of DNNs to be executed on the same platform.
IntPred can be used in a wide variety of autonomous driving systems to reduce the computational and energy costs of the object detection stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a technique that allows to save energy, reduce heat dissipation, and increase frame rate of object detection in Autonomous Driving software.
IntPred can save energy and reduce the cost of the platform, while keeping the same level of accuracy of the original object detection.

IntPred can save up to 70% of computations and up to 4.6× of frame rate, while keeping the accuracy of object detection comparable to the original DNN-based approach, and thus can be used to improve the energy efficiency of autonomous driving software.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for object detection in autonomous vehicles, it is possible to achieve the same accuracy with much less performance and power requirements, thus paving the way for the use of less powerful and cheaper platforms, while reducing energy consumption.
, in the case of Autonomous Driving systems, object detection can be performed at a lower performance and energy cost, without sacrificing accuracy.
, by leveraging on a specific domain, it is possible to reduce significantly the performance and energy overheads of object detection in Autonomous Driving software.
